screens.tally-list.title: Tallies
screens.tally-list.empty-body: A tally is a running account between you and one other person. You need someone to keep one with.
screens.tally-list.error-title: Your tallies could not be read
screens.tally-view.title: Tally
screens.tally-view.state-closing: Closing — no new activity until the balance settles
screens.tally-view.room-note: Credit they extended you — not value you hold
screens.tally-view.disclosure-note: What they chose to tell you. Anything absent may be withheld or simply not held.
screens.tally-view.requests-note: A request is a statement of what one of you thinks is owed. Only signed entries move the balance.
screens.tally-view.unreadable-title: This tally could not be read
screens.tally-history.title: History
screens.tally-history.unreadable-title: This history could not be read
screens.tally-history.empty-body: Entries appear here as value moves between you.
screens.tally-history.asked-note: Requests sit beside the ledger. Only signed entries move the balance.
screens.attention.empty-body: When somebody is waiting on you, it shows up here.
screens.position.unreadable-title: Your position could not be read
screens.position.empty-body: Once you hold a tally, what you are owed and what you owe appear here.
screens.position.estimate-note: An estimate, at your own rates, taking the less favourable direction.
screens.position.spending-note: Credit is somebody's willingness, not value you hold. Spending it elsewhere depends on reach.
disclosure.name: Name
screens.tally-view.unreachable-body: Nothing of theirs is answering. This is your record too, so everything here still reads.
screens.tally-view.pending-terms: Terms you proposed, not yet delivered
screens.tally-view.pending-entry: An entry you made, not yet delivered
screens.tally-view.pending-close: A close request, not yet delivered
screens.welcome.title: Taleus
screens.welcome.what-it-is: A tally is a running account between you and one other person.
screens.welcome.what-value-is: Value here is what people owe each other — not money sitting in an account somewhere.
screens.welcome.no-obligation: Setting up obliges you to nobody. You can look around first.
screens.choose-name.title: One thing to choose
screens.choose-name.identity-made: An identity has been set up for you. There was nothing for you to decide — no keys, no algorithm, no jargon.
screens.choose-name.on-this-device: It lives on this device. Before you hold anything of value, protecting it is worth doing.
screens.choose-name.ask: What should people you tally with see?
screens.choose-name.deferred: Nothing else is needed yet. Anything more is asked for when it matters, and you will be told who is asking.
screens.choose-name.needed: A name is needed before you can continue.
screens.choose-name.failed-title: That name could not be saved
screens.create-invitation.title: Invite someone
screens.create-invitation.no-recipient: You are setting out terms, not naming a person. Whoever accepts becomes the other party.
screens.create-invitation.note-label: A private note, so you can tell your invitations apart
screens.create-invitation.note-note: Yours only. It says nothing about who will respond.
screens.create-invitation.limit-label: How much are you willing to be owed?
screens.create-invitation.notice-label: How much notice before you can require settlement?
screens.create-invitation.yours-only: These are your numbers only. Whether they extend anything back is their decision, and they may extend nothing.
screens.create-invitation.unit-label: What does this tally count in?
screens.create-invitation.unit-permanent: This cannot be changed once the tally exists.
screens.create-invitation.agreement-note: Whoever accepts has to accept the same one, and can read it first.
screens.create-invitation.good-for-label: How long should the invitation stay good?
screens.create-invitation.failed-title: The invitation could not be made
screens.create-invitation.made-body: Nothing is owed yet, and there is no tally until somebody responds.
screens.create-invitation.share-not-buil: Sharing is not built yet — the token above is what would be handed over.
screens.review-invitation.title: An invitation
screens.review-invitation.who: {name} is inviting you to keep a tally.
screens.review-invitation.their-limit: They are willing to be owed
screens.review-invitation.their-notice: They want {count} days notice before they can require settlement
screens.review-invitation.nothing-disclo: You have disclosed nothing so far.
screens.review-invitation.about-you: What should they be told about you?
screens.review-invitation.your-terms: What are you willing to be owed by them?
screens.review-invitation.zero-is-fine: Zero is a normal answer. You can change it later.
screens.review-invitation.name-needed: A name is needed before you can accept.
screens.review-invitation.accepted: Accepted. They are told, and the tally opens once they agree.
screens.review-invitation.refused: Refused. They are told. This offer is finished, but they can come back with different terms.
screens.review-invitation.expired-body: It is no longer good. You can ask them for another.
screens.review-invitation.unreadable-tit: This invitation could not be read
screens.review-offer.title: Terms proposed
screens.review-offer.waiting-on-them: Sent. It is waiting on {name} now.
screens.review-offer.changed-none: Nothing changed from the last offer.
screens.review-offer.in-force-note: The tally keeps working on these while the offer is pending. Nothing is in limbo.
screens.review-offer.forming-note: There are no terms in force yet — this tally does not exist until you both sign the same offer.
screens.review-offer.unit-fixed: The unit is not negotiable — it is fixed for the life of the tally.
screens.review-offer.counter-note: Countering replaces the agreement rather than editing it: it is a new offer, and {name} has to agree to it before anything is settled.
screens.review-offer.counter-mine-limit: What you are willing to be owed
screens.review-offer.accepted: Signed. You both hold the same terms now.
screens.review-offer.countered: Sent. This is your offer now, and it is waiting on them.
screens.review-offer.none-body: No terms are waiting on you here.
screens.review-offer.unreadable-title: This offer could not be read
screens.review-offer.superseded-body: Both of you signed both offers. The one drafted later is the one in force, so you are both looking at the same answer.
screens.review-offer.superseded-onward: Either of you can propose again from here, or close the tally if this is not what you wanted.
screens.review-invitation.refused-onward: They can come back with different terms, and you can consider those on their own merits.
screens.pay-partner.title: Record value given
screens.pay-partner.memo-note: Enough that either of you will recognise it in a year.
screens.pay-partner.room-after: Room left of what they let you owe
screens.pay-partner.no-agreement-needed: This is your own act. They do not have to agree to receive value.
screens.pay-partner.beyond-title: This goes past what they agreed to
screens.pay-partner.beyond-body: It is {amount} beyond what {name} agreed to be owed. You can still do it — a pledge is your own promise to pay — but they are under no obligation to treat it as payment.
screens.pay-partner.recorded-body: Both of you see the same entry now. Nothing here can be edited or removed; a correction is a further entry, and both stay visible.
screens.pay-partner.nothing-changed: Nothing is owed differently than a moment ago. Trying again will not record it twice.
screens.create-request.title: Ask to be paid
screens.create-request.memo-note: In terms they will recognise when they see it.
screens.create-request.not-a-clock: A request does not tick. It stands until they answer it or you take it back — an unpaid bill does not stop existing because a month went by.
screens.create-request.obliges-nothing: It is your own statement of what you think is owed, and it obliges them to nothing by itself. Only signed entries move the balance.
screens.create-request.sent-body: They are asked to answer it. You can see where it stands, and how long it has been waiting.
screens.create-request.failed-title: The request could not be made
screens.request-view.title: A request
screens.request-view.no-clock: It does not lapse on its own. Time alone decides nothing.
screens.request-view.part-note: Nothing pretends the part settled the whole.
screens.request-view.not-a-commitment: This is what they say is owed. It is not yours until you give it — only signed entries move the balance.
screens.request-view.pay-note: The amount is theirs. Paying part is a normal answer, and you say which you are doing.
screens.request-view.decline-why: Say why, if you want to
screens.request-view.decline-note: Declining costs you nothing and moves nothing. They are told, and it stops waiting on you.
screens.request-view.withdraw-note: Asking was your act, and so is unasking. They see it withdrawn rather than vanishing.
screens.request-view.state-refused: Declined. They are told, and nothing moved.
screens.request-view.state-withdrawn: Taken back. They see it withdrawn.
screens.request-view.unreadable-title: This request could not be read
screens.close-tally.title: Close this tally
screens.close-tally.before-1: Nothing more builds up in either direction.
screens.close-tally.before-2: What is owed does not go away, and closing does not forgive it.
screens.close-tally.before-3: The tally ends when the balance reaches zero. Settling it is still allowed — that is the point.
screens.close-tally.no-permission: You do not need their agreement, and they cannot refuse it. They keep everything they are owed.
screens.close-tally.asked-by-me: You asked to close it on {date}.
screens.close-tally.asked-by-both: You both asked to close it. One request was already enough.
screens.close-tally.narrowed: Anything that moves the balance toward zero still goes through. Anything that would move it further from zero does not.
screens.close-tally.awaiting: It is waiting on settlement, not finished and not broken. It stays this way for as long as that takes.
screens.close-tally.overdue: That date has passed. Nothing has been added to the balance for it — what follows is between you and your agreement.
screens.close-tally.nothing-owed: Nothing is owed either way, so there is nothing to settle.
screens.close-tally.return-note: Handing back what you are owed brings the balance to zero and closes the tally. It is an ordinary act of giving value, and it lands in the history like any other.
screens.close-tally.writeoff-body: {amount} is holding this up. It is yours to give up, and nobody can do it for you.
screens.close-tally.writeoff-declined: Left as it is. You will not be asked again.
screens.close-tally.withdraw-note: While it is still closing you can change your mind, and the tally carries on as it was. Once the balance reaches zero it is final — carrying on means a new tally.
screens.close-tally.withdraw-blocked: It stays closing while their request stands.
screens.close-tally.unworkable-body: A tally is a record you keep together, so with their side gone there may be nothing you can add — including the settling that would let it close. Everything here stays readable.
screens.close-tally.unreadable-title: This tally could not be read
field.name: Name
field-inline.name: name
screens.settings.title: Settings
screens.settings.follows-you-note: On any device you add, without being set again.
screens.settings.this-device-note: A replacement phone starts fresh here.
screens.settings.only-language: The only one so far. More appear here as people contribute them — a half-translated app would be worse than this one.
screens.settings.quoted-note: What other people wrote — notes, names, what they said something was for — stays in their words, shown as a quote rather than translated.
screens.settings.agreement-note: A tally’s agreement stays in the language it was signed in; that text is the agreement. Where its publisher offers another language, you pick that version when the tally is formed.
screens.settings.display-unit-note: Each tally keeps counting in what it was agreed in — that is not yours to change. Where you have priced a unit, its equivalent appears beside the real figure, never instead of it.
screens.settings.no-rate: You have not said what {unit} is worth to you, so your overall figures cannot be estimated in it.
screens.settings.no-rate-fix: Give it a rate and they can be. Rates live with your exchange rates, per unit you hold.
screens.settings.unit-style-note: Both name the unit. The mark reads faster; the code is unmistakable.
screens.settings.about-me-note: What you hold, and what you have told each partner.
screens.settings.not-settings-owe: What you let a partner owe you is a term of that tally — agreed with them, and changed only by agreeing again.
screens.settings.not-settings-move: How value may move through your tallies is a permission you sign. It lives with your trading settings.
screens.settings.not-settings-why: Neither is a preference, so neither is here.
screens.settings.unreadable-title: Your settings could not be read
screens.profile.title: About me
screens.profile.held-note: None of this has gone anywhere. Writing it down tells nobody.
screens.profile.add-note: Worth filling in before somebody asks.
screens.profile.correction-body_one: {count} partner has the {field} you just changed. Sending them the new one is a statement you sign, so choose who gets it.
screens.profile.correction-body_other: {count} partners have the {field} you just changed. Sending them the new one is a statement you sign, so choose who gets it.
screens.profile.correction-send: Send to the ones I picked
screens.profile.correction-none: Nobody was sent anything. Your own record shows the new one either way.
screens.profile.correction-failed: Could not reach {names} just now. Nothing was sent to them; you can try again.
screens.profile.disclosures: What I have told each partner
screens.profile.sent-pending: Goes with the offer, if they sign it
screens.profile.unreadable-title: Your record could not be read
screens.disclosure.title: What we know of each other
screens.disclosure.sent-pending: Goes with the offer, if they sign it
screens.disclosure.tell-more-note: On this tally, as it stands. No new tally and no change to the terms — and they are told something arrived, so it is not filed somewhere they may never look.
screens.disclosure.they-say-note: Their words about themselves. Taleus has not checked any of it.
screens.disclosure.they-say-none: They have told you nothing but a name.
screens.disclosure.missing-body: You have no {fields} for them. Whether they would rather not say, or never wrote it down, does not reach you from here.
screens.disclosure.ask-note: Asking turns a silence into a yes or a no.
screens.disclosure.ask-why-placeholder: So they can judge it for themselves
screens.disclosure.refuse-note: They will see that you would rather not. What they do with that is theirs to decide.
screens.disclosure.not-held: You hold no {field} to send. Add it to your own record first.
screens.disclosure.answered-refused: You said you would rather not, {date}.
screens.disclosure.i-asked-refused: They would rather not, {date}. That is an answer.
screens.tally-terms.title: Terms
screens.tally-terms.coming-note: A reduction waits out the notice period before it applies. Until then the figure above is the one that governs.
screens.tally-terms.governs-new: Governs what happens from then on.
screens.tally-terms.governs-outstanding: What is already outstanding stays under the terms it was advanced under. A reduction does not reach back.
screens.tally-terms.stacking: Each reduction stacks on the future, not on the past, so both of these apply in turn.
screens.tally-terms.immediate: Nothing is outstanding, so there is no runway to shorten: this applies as soon as it is agreed.
screens.tally-terms.proposed-by-me: You proposed this on {date}. Waiting on {name}.
screens.tally-terms.proposed-by-them: {name} proposed this on {date}. You have not answered.
screens.tally-terms.proposed-note: Nothing about a proposal changes what either of you may do today.
screens.tally-terms.no-amendments: These are the terms you opened with. Neither of you has changed them.
screens.tally-terms.agreement-parameters: The figures above are what you filled in on it: {fields}.
screens.tally-terms.agreement-unavailabl: The agreement could not be fetched right now. The terms in force are your own record and are shown above regardless.
screens.tally-terms.who-note: What they told you about themselves. Taleus has not checked any of it, and what is not here could be either withheld or never written down.
screens.tally-terms.who-open: What we know of each other
screens.tally-terms.closed-note: This tally is no longer trading. Everything about it stays readable.
screens.tally-terms.unreadable-title: The terms could not be read
screens.entry-detail.title: Entry
screens.entry-detail.routed-in: Value reached you through this tally
screens.entry-detail.signed-me: You did. The party who gives the value signs the entry.
screens.entry-detail.signed-them: {name} did. The party who gives the value signs the entry.
screens.entry-detail.signed-network: Neither of you typed this one — a payment found its way through your tally and moved value on its own.
screens.entry-detail.answered-note: A request is the other party’s statement of what they think they are owed. This entry is what you signed against it.
screens.entry-detail.unsettled-note: This movement has not committed yet. The figure above is what it would come to; nothing is wrong, and it is not done.
screens.entry-detail.unrecognised: This is everything the record holds about it: the amount, which way it went, when, what was written down, who signed it, and whether it answered anything. Nothing in the history is anonymous.
screens.entry-detail.unreadable-title: This entry could not be read
screens.rates.title: What units are worth to me
screens.rates.private: These are yours. No partner sees them, and nobody else’s are ever applied to what you hold.
screens.rates.no-opinion: Taleus has no opinion about what anything is worth. Two people can value the same holding differently and both be right.
screens.rates.unpriced-why: You have never said what {unit} is worth to you, so it is not counted in your overall figures and no payment can route through it. The tallies themselves work exactly as they always did.
screens.rates.unpriced-fine: That is a coherent place to leave it. A unit you have no opinion about is one you can still hold and still settle in.
screens.rates.nothing-to-price: Everything you hold is in {unit}. There is nothing to price, and nothing here you need.
screens.rates.direction-note: The difference is your own reluctance to let them go, not a fee anyone charges you.
screens.rates.conservative: Your own figures use the less flattering of the two. There is no second set of numbers for looking at your position — these rates price your trades and your estimate alike.
screens.rates.scope: This is what {unit} is worth to you, on every tally you hold in it. It is not a per-partner judgement: if you need to value something differently depending on who you are dealing with, that is a different unit, not a different rate.
screens.rates.signed-instruction: You signed the instruction on {date}. What you signed is that, not each day’s figure.
screens.rates.source-unreachable: {source} could not be reached. The last figure it gave, from {date}, is still what value is converting at.
screens.rates.stale: You set this in {date} and have not looked at it since. It is not a dormant preference — value is still moving at it.
screens.rates.stale-note: That is about your own neglect, not about a market Taleus is watching for you.
screens.rates.enables-figures: These holdings count toward your overall estimate.
screens.rates.enables-movement: Value can move between your {unit} tallies and the rest when a payment needs it to.
screens.rates.figures-only: Counted in your figures, and nothing routes across it. Valuing something and permitting movement are different decisions.
screens.rates.movement-lives: Permitting movement is a signed permission, and it lives with your trading settings.
screens.rates.market-position-body: Plenty of people hold {unit}. Your rate is the price value actually converts at through you, and it stands until you change it. Nobody sees the number, but anyone trading against you finds it — including people watching that market far more closely than you are.
screens.rates.limit-how: Three ways to limit that: a margin wide enough to be safe, a ceiling on how much can accumulate this way — that one lives with your trading settings — or simply not pricing a unit you would rather not trade in.
screens.rates.circle: Only you and the people you use it with hold {unit}, so value priced in it only ever moves among you. A flat number is fine here and needs no source. There is nobody to arbitrage against — this is the safe case, not a lesser one.
screens.rates.basis-question: How should it be worked out?
screens.rates.basis-fixed-note: Simple, and it goes stale unless you come back to it.
screens.rates.basis-source-note: Plus or minus your own margin, so there is nothing to remember to maintain.
screens.rates.source-yours: You choose the source and the margin. The app never picks one for you, and you can change both.
screens.rates.movement-no: No — count it in my figures only
screens.rates.inverted: Parting with one cannot cost less than you will take for it.
screens.rates.unreadable-title: Your rates could not be read
screens.position.see-rates: What units are worth to me
screens.standing.title: A code others can take up
screens.standing.what: One set of terms, and anyone who takes it up gets their own tally with you on them. Not one answer — as many as there are people.
screens.standing.no-directory: Nobody can look you up. There is no directory, and there is not going to be one. You are findable only if you hand something out: printed by the till, on a card, in a message.
screens.standing.before-any: You can publish one before you have ever tallied with anybody.
screens.standing.limit: What I will let a stranger owe me
screens.standing.limit-note: Nothing is the ordinary answer, and it still works: whoever takes it up hands you value, it is recorded, and they spend it with you from there. You may think that worth a better price, since they have in effect lent you the money up front.
screens.standing.notice: Notice before I can require settlement
screens.standing.unit-note: Fixed once it is published, like any tally. Whoever takes it up gets this unit.
screens.standing.agreement-note: Whoever takes it up accepts the same one, and is free to refuse it.
screens.standing.binds-you: These are your numbers only. Whether anyone extends anything back is theirs to decide, tally by tally.
screens.standing.disclose: What everyone who takes it up will learn about you
screens.standing.disclose-public: This is effectively public. It goes to every person who takes this up — people you have not met and will not meet before they do. Anything you would not put on a card, leave out.
screens.standing.disclose-none: Nothing at all. That is allowed; they will see only what a tally cannot do without.
screens.standing.confirm: I understand this goes to everyone
screens.standing.hand-out-note: Print it, write it on a card, send it. Anyone with it can take it up until you withdraw it.
screens.standing.taken-up-note: Each is a separate tally from the moment it opened, and none of them is bound to what you published — you can negotiate any of them on its own.
screens.standing.taken-up-none: Nobody yet. It stands until you withdraw it.
screens.standing.withdraw-note: Withdrawing stops new people taking it up. It does nothing to the tallies that already came from it.
screens.standing.withdrawn-note: Nobody new can take this up. What came from it carries on.
screens.settings.standing-open: A code others can take up
screens.settings.standing-note: One set of terms anyone can accept, each becoming their own tally.
screens.notifications.title: What reaches you
screens.notifications.intro: Only things that need you ever arrive here. What happens on its own does not.
screens.notifications.phone-decides: Whether an interruption rings, buzzes or waits for your quiet hours is your phone’s decision, and you already have that where you expect it. What this app does is say honestly which is which, so that decision has something real to act on.
screens.notifications.class-signature-no: An offer to answer, terms proposed, a close asked for.
screens.notifications.class-asked: Someone has asked you to pay
screens.notifications.class-asked-note: Their statement of what they think you owe. It obliges you to nothing by itself.
screens.notifications.class-arrived-note: Value recorded, a request answered, something new disclosed to you.
screens.notifications.class-automatic-no: Never notifies, and that is not a setting. You authorised it, there is nothing for you to do, and it is there in the morning if you look.
screens.notifications.lock-screen-note: Your phone may light up on a table with other people around it. This is what they would see.
screens.notifications.lock-full-sample: “Mara’s Bike Shop asked you for $95 — 3 days”
screens.notifications.lock-full-warning: Choose this and amounts, names and balances appear where anyone standing there can read them.
screens.notifications.opening: Opening one takes you to the thing itself, not to a starting point you have to search from. If it has already been dealt with — on this device or any other of yours — it says so rather than sending you somewhere with nothing to do.
screens.notifications.together: Related things arrive together. A busy afternoon is not a dozen separate interruptions, and what you have already handled does not announce itself.
screens.notifications.participation: Taking part while you are not looking
screens.notifications.participation-what: Settling sometimes needs something of yours to answer. Your phone can be roused briefly to do that — it shows you nothing, and there is nothing to read or dismiss. It is not a message.
screens.notifications.participation-off: Leave this phone out of it
screens.notifications.participation-best: Best effort, never a promise. A phone decides for itself how much it will do while nobody is holding it, so some settling will pass you by.
screens.notifications.participation-decl: Nothing breaks. Your tallies settle when you open the app instead, and anything waiting is still waiting.
screens.notifications.always-on-have: Your home node stays on, so this does not rest on your phone.
screens.notifications.always-on-none: You have nothing that stays on. If you want your tallies to keep working regardless, the answer is a machine of yours that does — not a setting in here.
screens.notifications.always-on-where: That lives with your devices and your cadre.
screens.notifications.refused-cost: Nothing breaks, and you will not be asked again. What it costs: things wait for you to look, including requests with deadlines, and your phone may take part in settling less often than it otherwise would.
screens.notifications.refused-waiting: Anything that was waiting is still waiting when you open the app.
screens.notifications.refused-where: Your phone’s own settings are where this is turned back on.
screens.settings.notifications-note: What interrupts you, and what waits until you look.
